questions.q: Why is Daniel unhappy with his old way of studying?
choices: The science teacher is new
His sister is often busy
He has lost his textbook
Studying late makes him tired
questions.explanation: Daniel's old late-night routine leaves him tired before a test.

questions.q: What does Daniel learn by explaining an idea to his sister?
choices: Whether his sister enjoys science
Whether he really understands it
Whether his teacher likes his notes
Whether the next test will be easy
questions.explanation: Daniel checks his notes when he cannot explain the idea clearly.

questions.q: Why does Daniel turn off phone notifications?
choices: To study with fewer distractions
To make his phone battery last longer
To stop his sister from calling
To check the time of his test
questions.explanation: The phone notifications are switched off while he studies.

questions.q: Why is Daniel pleased although he makes two mistakes?
choices: He thinks the mistakes do not count
He does not need to study history
He feels calmer and has slept well
He has finished before all his classmates
questions.explanation: Paragraph three values a calmer routine and better sleep, not a perfect score.

questions.q: What does Daniel's plan for history suggest?
choices: Every subject is always the same
Only science needs short study sessions
His sister will help with history too
He can try a useful plan in another subject
questions.explanation: Daniel intends to use the new approach for history, changing it as needed.

questions.q: Why is answering questions without notes useful?
choices: It shows what Daniel can remember
It lets Daniel avoid the textbook
It means he can skip Monday's work
It changes the teacher's questions
questions.explanation: Working without answers helps him see what he has learned.

questions.q: You cannot explain an idea to a friend. What should you do?
choices: Move to a completely new topic
Read your notes and try again
Ask the friend to write your test
Ignore the difficult question
questions.explanation: Daniel checks his notes when an idea is not clear.

questions.q: A friend studies very late before every test. Which change could help?
choices: Study all evening without a break
Stop studying until test day
Plan short sessions across several days
Stay awake even later than usual
questions.explanation: Daniel changes from one exhausting evening to short sessions.

questions.q: Why might it be helpful to change a study plan?
choices: A useful plan does not have to be perfect
Teachers want a different plan every day
Only difficult subjects need planning
A good plan must never be repeated
questions.explanation: Daniel learns a useful plan can be adapted when necessary.

questions.q: Which description best fits Daniel's result?
choices: He learns all the science facts perfectly
He stops asking questions at school
He studies longer but sleeps less
He still makes mistakes but improves his routine
questions.explanation: His grade improves slightly, while his preparation and sleep improve too.
